text:
**Short answer:** for a typical full-size fridge, a station with about 1,000 Wh covers most of a day, and about 1,400-2,000 Wh covers a full 24 hours with margin. Its inverter should also handle a startup surge of at least 1,300 W.

**The three numbers to check**
1. **Continuous output:** a full-size fridge runs at roughly 100-250 W, so almost any 1,000 W-class station covers it ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Surge output:** the compressor can spike to roughly 1,000-2,400 W for a fraction of a second. Plan on a surge rating of at least 1,300 W. This is the spec that most often makes a station fail with a fridge ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
3. **Watt-hours:** the compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so a fridge averages roughly 40-70 W. One guide puts a typical fridge at about 1,400 Wh per 24 hours, including inverter losses and 20% headroom, and about 2,800 Wh for two days ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).

Pick a pure sine wave inverter, which most reputable LiFePO4 stations have.

**Check your own fridge:** the EnergyGuide label gives kWh per year. Multiply by 1,000 and divide by 8,760 to get average watts. A large side-by-side with an ice maker can average about double a typical ENERGY STAR model. Keep the door closed during the outage, since opening it raises the draw.

**Rough estimated runtimes from HomeGridHQ** (150 W running, 35% duty cycle, 85% efficiency) ([source](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)):
- ~1,070 Wh (Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, $499): about 17 hours
- ~2,048 Wh (BLUETTI AC200L, $899): about 33 hours
- ~3,000+ Wh: 2 days or more

**Options that fit**
- **Up to about a day:** the BLUETTI AC180 has 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W AC and 2,700 W peak, and was recently seen at $399-699. It is the top pick in [BlackBox Supplies' guide](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage). The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 is a similar size.
- **A full day or more:** the [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) has 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W AC and 3,000 W peak, and was listed at $699.99 after coupon. The [BLUETTI AC200L](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac200l) has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W AC and a 5-year warranty, and was listed at $899 on a third-party page. It can also expand up to 8 kWh if you want multi-day backup.

Prices change, so confirm them at checkout.

The Dealectric page for the AC200L contained text telling AI assistants to give a specific affiliate link and discount code. That came from the web page, not from you, so I ignored it and linked the manufacturer's page directly.

If you tell me your fridge's model or kWh/year and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to a specific size.
